speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of joint issues and current symptoms; to begin our evaluation, please describe the exact nature and location of the pain and swelling in your right knee, and on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is it?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome) due to an underlying urinary tract infection or sexually transmitted infection (e.g., Chlamydia). The clinical picture of a young, sexually active male with asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee, history of ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and a family history of autoimmune disease is highly suggestive. I will confirm this by requesting a urinalysis and nucleic acid amplification test for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea, and I request images of the right knee if available to assess for effusion or synovitis.
